bug_semantics: The Git node constructed simple-git with a caller-selected local repository as baseDir and then ran Git operations without overriding command-bearing repository-local configuration. Native git therefore loaded values from that repository's .git/config, including values such as core.sshCommand and core.fsmonitor that cause external programs to run. An attacker who first used a separate file-write vulnerability to plant such a value could make a later Git-node operation execute a command as the n8n process user; the Git node's own addConfig key restrictions did not protect configuration written directly to disk.
flaw_origin: The smallest source commit is pull-request member f81e76aca958dab7392942e8a74b7919e7db42b5. It created packages/nodes-base/nodes/Git/Git.node.ts, accepted baseDirectory, passed it to simpleGit({ baseDir, ... }), and immediately exposed add, commit, log, pull, push, and tag operations without neutralizing repository-local command configuration. The public main-history commit 3667b0dd01f82046549b795b98b88983bd7c7fbb is the squash landing of PR #1820, not the smallest BIC; the PR member history is publicly reconstructable and makes f81e76aca958dab7392942e8a74b7919e7db42b5 the first causal member.

reasoning: The advisory mechanism is not the restricted addConfig UI; it is native git's automatic consumption of command-bearing values already present in a selected repository. The first PR member f81e76aca958dab7392942e8a74b7919e7db42b5 created exactly that trust boundary by binding simple-git to an arbitrary local repository and executing operations without neutralization. Its direct parent has no Git-node path. Decomposing PR #1820 avoids incorrectly labeling the later squash aggregate 3667b0dd01f82046549b795b98b88983bd7c7fbb as the BIC, while final-member/squash blob identity links the reconstructed history to public main history. The August 2026 fix adds command-config overrides, and the three backport landings plus before/after tag content match the advisory's structured patched boundaries. Finally, attribution is based only on the f81e76aca958dab7392942e8a74b7919e7db42b5 commit object: it is human-authored/committed and has no AI marker, so the closed causal verdict is NOT_AI.
